# tilecache

tilecache rasterises vector map sources into PNG tiles and serves them from a
local disk cache. It is the tile backend behind the trail-mapping app.

## Layout

- src/tile - the renderer, the glyph atlas, and the on-disk cache.
- src/server.ts - the HTTP entry point and the tile route.
- tests - vitest specs, one per subsystem.

## Running locally

    npm install
    npm run build
    npm test

history.task: Serve a transparent png for tiles that have no source data
history.summary: Missing tiles used to come back as a JSON error body with a 200, which the mobile client drew as a grey block. A tile with no source data is now a cached transparent png, so the map shows the basemap underneath instead of a hole.

history.task: Cap the on-disk tile cache with an LRU eviction pass
history.summary: The disk cache grew without bound and filled the box twice last month. Eviction is now least-recently-used against a configurable byte cap, checked every thousand writes rather than on every write, which kept the added latency under a millisecond.

history.task: Add a CI job that renders a golden tile and diffs it against the reference
history.summary: CI now renders one golden tile per zoom band and compares it to a checked-in reference image, failing the job when more than a tenth of a percent of the pixels move. That is what started catching the empty output nobody could reproduce by hand.

history.task: Renderer specs are green on my laptop but the CI job keeps producing blank tiles
history.summary: Chased the blank output down to the on-disk glyph atlas. Under the default pool, two worker threads share one cache directory, and whichever finishes second truncates the atlas the first one is still reading, so the renderer draws nothing. The atlas writer now stages to a per-process temp file and renames it into place. Reproducing the original failure by hand needs the recorded fixture set and a run pinned to forked workers with file parallelism switched off; the default invocation hides it behind thread scheduling.

tests.summary: 14 renderer cases pass and the blank-tile regression reproduces on demand instead of once in twenty runs

history.task: Investigate the slow first tile request after a deploy
history.summary: The first request after a deploy pays for the whole glyph atlas build, which is about 900ms at zoom 14. Prebuilding it in the deploy step would fix it, but the deploy pipeline is owned by another team, so this is parked with a ticket rather than solved here.

commands.summary: bench harness crashed on the cold cache path

history.task: Write the tile coordinate scheme into the readme
history.summary: Wrote the slippy-map coordinate scheme and the zoom clamp into the readme, because every new contributor asks the same question about which way y counts and what happens past zoom 18.

# tilecache

tilecache rasterises vector map sources into PNG tiles and serves them from a
local disk cache. It is the tile backend behind the trail-mapping app.

## Layout

- src/tile - the renderer, the glyph atlas, and the on-disk cache.
- src/server.ts - the HTTP entry point and the tile route.
- tests - vitest specs, one per subsystem.

## Running locally

    npm install
    npm run build
    npm test

## Tile coordinates

Routes use the slippy-map scheme, z/x/y, with y counted from the north. Zoom is
clamped to 0..18; anything past 18 is served by upscaling the z18 tile rather
than by rendering, because the source data carries no detail beyond that.
